D000779.s: Drugs that block nerve conduction when applied locally to nerve tissue in appropriate concentrations. They act on any part of the nervous system and on every type of nerve fiber. In contact with a nerve trunk, these anesthetics can cause both sensory and motor paralysis in the innervated area.

D000928.s: Mood-stimulating drugs used primarily in the treatment of affective disorders and related conditions. Several monoamine oxidase inhibitors are useful as antidepressants apparently as a long-term consequence of their modulation of catecholamine levels.

D001314.s: Act of listening for sounds within the body.

D001844.s: Transmission of sound waves through vibration of bones in the skull to the inner ear (cochlea). By using bone conduction stimulation and by bypassing any outer ear or middle ear abnormalities, hearing thresholds of the cochlea can be determined.

D002342.s: Branch of the common carotid artery which supplies the exterior of the head, the face, and the greater part of the neck.

D002603.s: A group of four British islands and several islets in the English Channel off the coast of France. They are known to have been occupied prehistorically. They were a part of Normandy in 933 but were united to the British crown at the time of the Norman Conquest in 1066.

D002676.s: The child who is not wanted by one or both parents.

D003051.s: The part of the inner ear (labyrinth) that is concerned with hearing. It forms the anterior part of the labyrinth, as a snail-like structure that is situated almost horizontally anterior to the vestibular labyrinth.

D003190.s: Providing for the full range of dental health services for diagnosis, treatment, follow-up, and rehabilitation of patients.

D003482.s: Board, room, and other personal assistance services generally provided on a long term basis. It excludes regular medical care.

D003954.s: Organized services for the purpose of providing diagnosis to promote and maintain health.

D004065.s: Congenital structural abnormalities of the digestive system.

D004551.s: A hinge joint connecting the forearm to the ARM.

D005318.s: The heart of the fetus of any viviparous animal. It refers to the heart in the postembryonic period and is differentiated from the embryonic heart (heart/embryology) only on the basis of time.

D005624.s: The bone that forms the frontal aspect of the skull. Its flat part forms the forehead, articulating inferiorly with the nasal bone and the cheek bone on each side of the face.

D005750.s: The liquid secretion of the stomach mucosa consisting of hydrochloric acid (gastric acid); pepsinogens; intrinsic factor; gastrin; mucus; and the bicarbonate ion (bicarbonates). (From Best & Taylor's Physiological Basis of Medical Practice, 12th ed, p651)

D006188.s: Infection with nematodes of the genus haemonchus, characterized by digestive abnormalities and anemia similar to that from hookworm infestation.

D007639.s: Infectious diseases of cattle, sheep, and goats, characterized by blepharospasm, lacrimation, conjunctivitis, and varying degrees of corneal opacity and ulceration.

D007855.s: Poisoning that results from chronic or acute ingestion, injection, inhalation, or skin absorption of LEAD or lead compounds.

D008205.s: A lymphatic disease characterized by inflammation of lymphatic vessels.

D008414.s: Inflammation of the udder in cows.

D009026.s: All deaths reported in a given population.

D009475.s: Neurons which conduct nerve impulses to the central nervous system.

D009912.s: Disorders of the mouth attendant upon non-oral disease or injury.

D011629.s: Development of sexual maturation in boys and girls at a chronological age that is 2.5 standard deviations below the mean age at onset of puberty in the population.

D012934.s: The separation of individuals or groups resulting in the lack of or minimizing of social contact and/or communication. This separation may be accomplished by physical separation, by social barriers and by psychological mechanisms. In the latter, there may be interaction but no real communication.

D013036.s: An epileptic syndrome characterized by the triad of infantile spasms, hypsarrhythmia, and arrest of psychomotor development at seizure onset. The majority present between 3-12 months of age, with spasms consisting of combinations of brief flexor or extensor movements of the head, trunk, and limbs.

D013043.s: Various branches of surgical practice limited to specialized areas.

D013986.s: Toxicoses caused by toxic substances secreted by the salivary glands of ticks; include tick paralysis (neurotropic toxin), sweating sickness (dermotropic toxin), and Rhipicephalus appendiculatus toxicosis (leukotropic toxin).

D014727.s: Those procedures designed to widen the zone of attached gingiva and deepen the vestibular depth which will facilitate the clearance of the area for natural food passage, and provide access for toothbrushing and interdental stimulation.

D015908.s: A technique for assisting the circulation by decreasing the afterload of the left ventricle and augmenting the diastolic pressure.

D016866.s: Infections with bacteria of the family bacteroidaceae.

D018187.s: A psychological theory based on dimensions or categories used by a given person in describing or explaining the personality and behavior of others or of himself. The basic idea is that different people will use consistently different categories.

D018213.s: Neoplasms composed of bony tissue, whether normal or of a soft tissue which has become ossified. The concept does not refer to neoplasms located in bones.

D018266.s: A malignant tumor composed of cells showing differentiation toward sebaceous epithelium. The tumor is solitary, firm, somewhat raised, more or less translucent, and covered with normal or slightly verrucose epidermis. It may be yellow or orange. The face and scalp are the commonest sites.

D019683.s: The percent frequency with which a dominant or homozygous recessive gene or gene combination manifests itself in the phenotype of the carriers. (From Glossary of Genetics, 5th ed)

D020500.s: Works consisting of presentations of numerical data on particular subjects.

D022142.s: Vesicles derived from the golgi apparatus containing material to be released at the cell surface.

D029424.s: A disease of chronic diffuse irreversible airflow obstruction. Subcategories of COPD include chronic bronchitis and pulmonary emphysema.

D033283.s: The freedom of patients to review their own medical, genetic, or other health-related records.

D045170.s: Regions of the chromatin or DNA that bind to the nuclear matrix. They are found in intergenic dna, especially flanking the 5' ends of genes or clusters of genes.

D047851.s: Terrorism on September 11, 2001 against targets in New York, the Pentagon in Virginia, and an aborted attack that ended in Pennsylvania.

D050217.s: The conjugation of exogenous substances with various hydrophilic substituents to form water soluble products that are excretable in urine. Phase II modifications include glutathione conjugation; acylation; and amination. Phase II enzymes include glutathione transferase and glucuronosyltransferase.

D052138.s: Genes whose abnormal expression, or mutation are associated with the development, growth, or progression of neoplasms.

D053704.s: Non-invasive, endoscopic imaging by use of video capsule endoscopes to perform examination of the gastrointestinal tract, especially the small bowel.

D055423.s: A course of food intake that is high in FATS and low in carbohydrates. This diet provides sufficient proteins for growth but insufficient amount of carbohydrates for the energy needs of the body. A ketogenic diet generates 80-90% of caloric requirements from fats and the remainder from proteins.

D057825.s: Methods of comparing two or more samples on the same two-dimensional gel electrophoresis gel.

D058011.s: A statistical tool for detecting and modeling gene-gene interactions. It is a non-parametric and model-free approach.

D058226.s: Lesions formed within the walls of arteries associated with deposits of fat and other substances that accumulate in the lining of the artery wall.

D063866.s: Unauthorized access to personal information to obtain medical care or drugs, or to submit fraudulent billing for services. (from https://oig.hhs.gov/fraud/medical-id-theft/index.asp)

D066252.s: Attributes and experiences that influence an individual's personality, attitudes, and lifestyle, which are derived from the social values and/or behavior of the groups to which an individual belongs, or aspires to belong.

D000069497.s: The process by which life began.

D000074608.s: Zinc finger domains (named for myeloid, Nervy and DEAF-1) that occur in a variety of eukaryotic proteins, including RUNT-related transcription factor 1 .

D000077432.s: An opioid analgesic, MU opioid receptor agonist, and noradrenaline reuptake inhibitor that is used in the treatment of moderate to severe pain, and of pain associated with diabetic neuropathies.

D000088724.s: Advocacy for the preservation, restoration, or improvement of the natural environment. It aims to reduce the impact of human activities on the earth and its inhabitants.
